title: SwiftUI iOS Rules
summary: Project rules for SwiftUI apps: @Observable models, NavigationStack routing, async/await with actors, previews and XCTest coverage.
description: These rules set the shape of a SwiftUI codebase: thin views, observable models that own state, and navigation driven by data. They steer an agent away from patterns that fight the framework.
They also address Swift concurrency and testing, so network calls stay off the main thread and each model can be exercised without launching the UI.
useWhen: You start a SwiftUI iOS app
Views contain networking and parsing code
Concurrency warnings appear after enabling strict checking
body:
# Project rules: SwiftUI for iOS

## Views and state
- Keep views small and declarative. Move logic into an `@Observable` model marked `@MainActor`. Use `@State` to own a model, `@Bindable` for bindings, `@Environment` for shared dependencies.
- Extract a subview when a body passes about 40 lines. Avoid `AnyView`; prefer generics and `@ViewBuilder`.
- Use stable `Identifiable` ids in `ForEach`; never index-based identity for mutable lists.

## Navigation
- Use `NavigationStack` with a typed path and `navigationDestination(for:)`. Present sheets from state, not from imperative calls.

## Concurrency and data
- Use async/await. Call services from `.task { }`, which cancels with the view. Isolate shared mutable state in an `actor`. Make model types `Sendable`.
- Never force-unwrap or use `try!` outside tests. Surface failures as state the view renders.
- Put networking behind a protocol so tests can inject a fake. Keep secrets in Keychain.

## Quality
- Every view has a `#Preview` with sample data, including an empty and an error case.
- Write XCTest or Swift Testing tests for each model. Add accessibility labels and support Dynamic Type.
- Run `swift-format lint` and `xcodebuild test` on a simulator before finishing.

example.prompt: Show a list of recipes with a detail screen and pull to refresh
example.result: The agent adds a RecipesModel, a NavigationStack with typed routes, refreshable async loading and tests using a fake service.

faq.question: Does it target the Observation framework?
faq.answer: Yes, it assumes @Observable. For older deployment targets, swap in ObservableObject and keep the other rules.

faq.question: Which test framework?
faq.answer: Either XCTest or Swift Testing works; pick one per target and keep to it.

access: Instructions only; it does not read or run anything by itself
